_comment: SKELETON INTAKE — trade-agnostic. Copy this over client-intake.json, paste a trade preset from brief-presets.txt into _brief, then fill the content. Every _-prefixed key (including these _comment notes) is stripped by config.ts and NEVER renders. Read INTAKE-SPEC.txt before filling.

_brief._comment: DIRECTION, never content. config.ts strips this whole block. Two kinds of keys: (1) ENGINE OVERRIDES read by variants.mjs; (2) CREATIVE DIRECTION in designDirection{} read by Cursor/you. Leave an engine override empty to let the seeded engine choose (more portfolio variety); set it to LOCK that axis.

layoutVariants._comment: Force a variant per section, or leave empty for the seeded pick. Valid names are in VARIANTS.txt and enforced by check-catalogue.mjs. story, testimonials and footer have ONE layout each — they have no variant axis, so no key here.

_brief._engine_key_reference: designKit: ledger|workshop|coast|press|signal (this also picks the two typefaces, loaded per-kit by astro.config.mjs) | surface: flat|tint|warm | bandSection: <a section key present in `sections`> OR none | variantSeed: any string (change to reshuffle the whole look)

designDirection._comment: Read by Cursor as creative guidance; ignored by the engine. This is what makes a painter feel different from a tiler. Fill from a brief-presets.txt preset, then tune per client.

_brief._layoutVariantsNote: Only hero and header have rendering variants. hero: typographic|split-media|fullbleed|editorial (the last two need features.hasPhotos). header: standard|minimal|centered. Empty = the engine seeds it from the client name.

_meta._comment_domain: REQUIRED: replace with the client's real domain. Seeds the engine (with business.name) and sets the canonical/sitemap URL.

_comment_sections: Controls WHICH sections render and the base order. hero+services pin near the top; faq/faqs+contact pin to the bottom; the rest is seeded-shuffled unless _brief.sectionsLocked is true. Remove a key to drop that section.

pages._comment: Per-page switches. A page turned on with no content redirects home instead of building.

contact.email: REQUIRED — the dev banner flags this even for phone-first clients.

style._comment: Client's real brand colours. ONLY brand, brandDark and accent are required — every other colour on the site (page paper, body ink, muted text, borders, card, eyebrow ink, on-dark text, the section band, and the text colour on every CTA) is DERIVED from these by src/lib/palette.mjs and contrast-checked at build time. Do not paste colours from another client's intake to 'fill it in' — that is how a landscaper's greens ended up in a painter's hero. brandDark must be genuinely dark (WCAG luminance <= 0.183) or the colour band self-suppresses. Optional overrides, only when the client insists: highlight, bg, card, ink, muted, border, surfaceAlt, accentInk, accentOndark, brandSecondaryInk, onDark, band. Run `npm run check:universal` to see the resolved palette and its contrast report.

hero._comment: heading + headingTint (the coloured tail) + subhead + primaryCta are the minimum. stats[]: up to 4 {value,label} shown as a strip under the hero — REAL numbers only, nothing derived or rounded up. rating: {score,scale,line,href} anchors the `editorial` variant. image+imageAlt only when features.hasPhotos is true; without a photo the engine routes to `typographic` and generates a motif from the palette + business.trade. motif: swatch|grid|contour|circuit|strata overrides that pick.
hero._comment_stats: stats[] {value,label} — REAL numbers only. Gates hero/stat-lede, where stats[0] becomes the lede and stats[1..3] the strip beneath. No stats, no variant: it has no placeholder state.

services._comment: items[] drives the homepage hero card row (title + description + includes[] + optional price + optional href). For rich per-service DETAIL pages (/services/[slug]) add records to src/data/services.ts instead.
services.heading: Services

items._comment: EXAMPLE item — duplicate per service. description is the short card line. longDescription + includes[] (2+) gate list-detail. image is gated by features.hasPhotos and gates split-scroll (needs one on EVERY service) and feature-lead (needs one on the LEAD service). featured:true marks the service that leads in feature-lead — first true wins, else items[0].

tiers._comment: Optional pricing/frequency tiers with an intensity bar (intensity of `of`). Remove the whole block if unused.

usage._comment: Read by the `areas` section (v3.16) — it used to live inside Story, so switching story off silently removed the suburb coverage. featured[] become the homepage chips; items[] is the full list for /areas.
usage.heading: Service areas

whyUs._comment: Bare array OR this object form. items[]: title + description. type 'process' unlocks whyUs/process-rail — set it ONLY when the items are a real sequence (test: can they be reordered without losing meaning? if yes they are a list). pairs[] {them,us} unlocks contrast-pair and must come from the client, never be invented. trust[] is the optional strip above the list.

cards._comment: Standard card: title + description. Emoji cards were removed in v3.16 (DESIGN-LIBRARY B6 bans emoji as section icons). Badge card: {title, type:'badges', badges:[]}.

story._comment_process: process[] {title,body} — a genuine sequence. Automatically suppressed if whyUs renders process-rail, so the page never shows two numbered sequences.

testimonials._comment: Bare array OR {eyebrow,heading,items[]}. NEVER invent these — real, sourced reviews only, or leave empty.

recentJobs._comment: Optional 'recent jobs' strip. Copy lives here (heading/subhead); the actual entries + photos live in src/data/recent-jobs.ts. Empty by default — the section self-hides.
recentJobs.heading: Recent jobs

gallery._comment: Optional /gallery copy. Entries + photos live in src/data/gallery.ts. Real paired photos only.

contactSection._comment: emailSubject overrides the form email subject (defaults to 'New enquiry — <business>'). messagePlaceholder overrides the textarea placeholder.

features._comment: hasPhotos MUST be an explicit boolean and only flips true when REAL files exist in public/images. It gates hero split-media/fullbleed and services split-scroll/feature-lead — those variants become unavailable, not broken.

seo._keywordsNote: No meta keywords tag — dead since 2009 and it only showed competitors your targets. Keep a keyword list in your own notes for copy and service-area planning.
seo._comment_ogImage: Leave empty until a real file exists in public/. A wrong path is worse than none — social scrapers cache a 404 hard, so the link preview stays broken for days after you fix it.

analytics._comment: Leave provider empty for no analytics. plausible + umami are cookieless (no consent banner). ga4 sets cookies and triggers the consent banner under Consent Mode v2.

agency._comment: Build credit in the client footer. Defaults to Kova Digital, with the anchor phrasing chosen per client so dozens of sites do not share one identical footer link. credit.enabled:false removes it (what a white-label fee buys). credit.rel set to nofollow keeps the referral traffic without passing link equity. credit.label overrides the wording entirely.

_serviceAreasNote: Service-area pages. A suburb gets its own page ONLY when it carries content that could not be pasted onto the next suburb: an intro of 60+ words plus at least one anchor — a job in jobs[], a note[] of 20+ words about local housing stock, or a sourced review from that suburb. Everything else stays a list entry in usage.items, which is honest: the suburb is served, there just isn't a page's worth to say yet. The build fails if two area pages are 70%+ the same text, because near-identical suburb pages are a doorway site. Fields: name, slug, intro, heading, metaDescription, services[], jobs[{title,street,detail}], note, testimonialQuote + testimonialName + testimonialSourceUrl, nearby[].
_comment_serviceAreas: serviceAreas[] builds a PAGE per suburb, each needing a 60+ word unique intro. Twenty thin pages is a doorway-site pattern. Leave empty and keep suburbs in usage.items[] unless there is genuinely a page's worth to say.
